objective: Make all text file I/O in the four scoped workflow files explicitly use UTF-8 and verify the completed encoding-only change with interpreter-portable acceptance commands.
requirements: Add encoding="utf-8" to every text-mode Path.read_text, Path.write_text, open, Path.open, and os.fdopen call in the four scoped files.
Exclude low-level os.open calls that create raw file descriptors because they are not text I/O and do not accept an encoding argument.
Preserve existing workflow behavior and pure-ASCII artifact bytes while changing only the selected text encoding.
Maintain focused regression coverage for static source auditing, non-ASCII round trips through orchestrator helpers, and ADR template generation.
Use the orchestrator-supported {python} placeholder in every Python acceptance command so validation invokes its own interpreter on Windows and other platforms.
Leave .ai/hooks/pre_tool_use.py, .ai/hooks/post_tool_use.py, _support.py, the CI matrix, and json.dumps ensure_ascii behavior unchanged.

files_to_modify.purpose: Specify UTF-8 for every orchestrator text read, write, append, and text stream created from a file descriptor.
Specify UTF-8 for all review-package text reads and writes.
Specify UTF-8 when reading workflow context and constitution text.
Specify UTF-8 when reading workflow event and implementation-note text.

files_to_create.purpose: Provide AST-based and behavioral regression tests for explicit UTF-8 text I/O, Unicode artifact round trips, ASCII compatibility, and ADR output.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Every text-mode read_text, write_text, open, Path.open, and os.fdopen call in the four scoped files explicitly specifies encoding="utf-8", while raw descriptor-only os.open calls remain excluded.
The orchestrator's artifact helpers preserve an em dash, curly quote, and non-Latin character through write/read round trips, and pure-ASCII output remains byte-compatible.
ADR creation produces a Supersedes line containing the literal UTF-8 em dash without a replacement character or question-mark substitution.
The complete repository unittest suite passes on the validation interpreter with a non-empty, parseable test count.

constraints: Use only the Python standard library.
Do not change behavior other than explicitly selecting UTF-8 for text I/O.
Do not change platform-dependent newline translation; it is pre-existing and outside TASK-006.
Do not refactor, rename, reformat, or restructure unrelated code.
Do not change json.dumps ensure_ascii behavior.
Do not weaken, delete, or modify existing tests.
Restrict implementation changes to the four named workflow files and the declared focused test file.
Retain Python 3.9 compatibility; the existing CI matrix remains responsible for exercising Python 3.9 and 3.12.
Workflow infrastructure files are authorized by their explicit declaration in this plan, consistent with the constitution and ADR-0004.
risks: The previous plan's implementation scope and testing approach were structurally sound; validation failed solely because every acceptance command used the non-functional bare Windows python alias instead of the required {python} placeholder, so this replan changes the verification contract rather than prescribing different code.
A naive textual count can misclassify low-level os.open as text I/O; the AST audit must distinguish raw descriptor creation from decoded text streams.
Behavioral tests alone cannot detect omitted encoding arguments on hosts whose locale is already UTF-8, so the static source audit is required.
Whole-file byte comparisons can fail on Windows because text-mode writes translate newlines to CRLF; Unicode byte assertions must avoid treating that out-of-scope behavior as an encoding failure.

The test helper _support.py retains locale-dependent text I/O outside the declared scope, so non-ASCII fixtures must be created through the orchestrator helpers or explicit UTF-8 operations in the focused test.
The working tree contains unrelated changes, so implementation must preserve them and touch only the declared paths.
test_strategy: Use an AST-based audit over all four scoped files to enumerate text-stream calls, require a literal UTF-8 encoding argument, guard against vacuous matching, and verify os.open is not incorrectly given encoding.
Exercise orchestrator context and task-artifact helpers in isolated temporary task directories with an em dash, curly quote, and Japanese text, checking both decoded values and UTF-8 bytes.
Exercise ADR creation through the real orchestrator path in an isolated directory and inspect the generated Supersedes line and raw bytes.
Verify pure-ASCII artifacts remain ASCII byte-for-byte.
Run the focused test classes with {python}, then run full unittest discovery with {python}; rely on the unchanged CI matrix for separate Python 3.9 and 3.12 execution.
